thought: Fire's caught proper now, and there's a roof half over my head. First day nearly done and I'm still breathing — that'll do for a start.
diary: First proper day ashore, and I'm writing this by firelight with bracken up to my knees. Got the frame of a lean-to up and a ring of stones round the fire, and tonight, God willing, I won't freeze for it. Cut my hand on something in the wreckage this morning — nothing that won't mend. Tired in a way I don't think sleep alone will fix, but the fire's caught and holding, and that's the whole of my luck today and I'll take it. Tomorrow: the roof, before the weather remembers where it left off.

thought: A fishing boat went by out past the reef tonight, lit up and none the wiser I was here. Didn't wave, didn't shout — too far, too dark. Banked the fire and lay down hungry, thinking on it.
diary: A boat passed this evening, out beyond the reef — the first sign of another living soul since I came ashore. I watched its lights a good while before they went. Didn't call out; it would never have carried, and I hadn't the strength to make a fool of myself for nothing. Belly's empty and won't let me forget it, but the fire's banked and should hold till morning. Next time a boat comes by, I want smoke enough to be seen, not just watched for.

thought: Woke dry under a proper roof for the first time — bed of pine boughs, no ground-chill in my bones. Dragging poles now for a signal tripod. That boat won't slip past me twice.
diary: Slept the whole night under a finished roof and didn't once wake shivering — small thing to be proud of, but I'll take my pride where I find it out here. The dog was at the treeline again this morning, close enough to see her properly this time: thin but not starving, watching me the way I watch the tide. Didn't push it. Today I want poles for a signal tripod, dry wood packed in the middle, so if another boat comes by there's more than moonlight to see me by. Belly's still asking questions I can't fully answer yet, but one thing at a time.

thought: Signal tripod's stood and packed with dry wood — one good thing done. Now it's withies and a funnel mouth for the fish trap, so I'm not living meal to meal on whatever the shore gives up.
Bone-tired and glad of it — fish trap set, two snares out, wood going up off the wet ground. And I put scraps down for Nell today. She ate them once I'd stepped well back.
diary: A day's proper work behind me and my arms know it. Fish trap's in the water, two snares laid along the warren path, wood stacking up on the rack before the weather turns. Best of it though: I set scraps out for the dog and backed off, and she came and ate them, watching me the whole time like I might change my mind about being harmless. Didn't try to touch her — that's a day for another time. Still just the two of us out here, but it feels a little less like just the one.

thought: Fire's gone to cold ash and my belly won't let me sleep proper. Fog's thick tonight. Come first light I'm at that trap and those snares before anything else — they'd better have earned their keep.

Belly's quiet again, thank God, though I couldn't rightly tell you what settled it. Fire's still cold ash and wants relighting before I do another thing. Fog's sitting low this morning — can't see past the treeline.
diary: Third day, and I made it through a hungry night without it turning into anything worse. Whatever I managed between the trap, the snares and what's left in my hands has quieted my stomach, if not answered every question about tomorrow. Fire's out again — that's twice now, and I'm getting tired of relighting it from scratch each morning. Fog's thick enough I can't see the shore from the lean-to. Feeling the quiet of this place more today than I have — no one to grumble to about any of it but myself, and Nell, who isn't much for conversation yet. Fire first, then the woodpile cover, then I'll see what the fog gives up.

thought: Piling leaf litter over the debris hut, arm-deep, and it's coming on well. But that fire's been cold since last night and I keep telling myself I'll see to it after this next handful of leaves. No more excuses — soon as this pile's done.
Debris hut's finished, bed and all, and the fire's caught proper this time. Legs won't hold me a minute longer, though — sitting here watching the flame do the work for once.
diary: Second shelter done today — a proper debris hut, ridge and ribs and a deep bed of leaves, built with my own two hands and whatever the wood gave me. Fire's lit again and holding, third time of asking. I'm wrung out in a way that's more satisfaction than exhaustion, if that makes any sense to anyone but me. Tomorrow there's still that third snare wanting a noose, and the woodpile could do with its cover before the weather changes its mind about being kind. For now I'll sit by the fire a while and let my hands rest.

thought: Ash banked over the coals, belly grumbling a little, throat drier than I'd like. Water's the thing I've not properly sorted yet — stream water straight down has never once agreed with a sailor's stomach. Sleep first, mind on it tomorrow.

Weak in the knees this morning, proper weak, stripping brambles with shaking hands. I've been building like a man with a full belly and I haven't got one. Today's for food and nothing else until I'm right again.
diary: Fourth day, and hunger's caught up with me properly — weak enough this morning that the berry bushes swam a bit before my eyes. I've been so set on the building that I've let the eating slide, and that's a fool's bargain out here. The trap and the snares haven't given me much yet, whatever the reason, so it's berries and whatever else I can find with my own two hands today. No more roofs, no more tripods, till I've put something solid back in my stomach. Nell was watching from the treeline again this morning — I daresay she knows hunger better than I do.
